quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: How do sudden wind gusts affect vehicles on highways?

options.text: They only affect large vehicles.
They only cause visibility problems.
They can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind can affect all drivers. It reduces visibility by blowing dirt and dust on the road. It can also physically push a vehicle off course.

questions.question: What must you do before turning right on a red light?

options.text: Slow down and go if the way is clear. You do not need to stop.
Come to a complete stop. Look both ways. Let pedestrians and other traffic go first.
Speed up because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop. Look both ways. Let pedestrians and other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk. You must yield to all pedestrians and cross traffic before turning.

questions.question: What speed should you drive when merging onto a freeway?

options.text: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter a freeway at or near the speed of traffic. Do not drive faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
Divided highway starts. Slow down to 35 mph.
Merge ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
Winding road ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road curves to the right. Slow down to the safe speed shown (35 mph).

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is safe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Your driving speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous. It may frustrate drivers behind you, causing them to make unsafe passing moves. Drive with the flow of traffic within the legal speed limit.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, what must you do?

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half a lane.
Pass the motorcycle using the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has the same rights as any other vehicle. Give the rider a full lane width. Even though there may seem to be room to share a lane, motorcycles need space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: You meet an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road. What must you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
Tell the other vehicle to pull over.
Turn on your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, both vehicles must have at least half the road. This gives both drivers enough space to safely pass each other.

questions.question: When backing up on a two-lane road, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the way is clear before backing.
Turn your head to look back before and while backing.
Stop and signal if you see a vehicle approaching from behind.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head to see behind your vehicle before and while backing. Check that the way is clear of traffic.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass if you are in the lane next to the solid line.
No one can pass from either direction.
You can pass if you are in the lane next to the broken line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if you are in the lane next to the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can pass. A solid line means you cannot. If you are next to the broken line, you can pass. If you are next to the solid line, you cannot pass.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop before crossing.
Slow down and go carefully.
Wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for other traffic, and proceed with caution.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn the bicyclist you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a bicycle, slow down and give them plenty of space. Bicyclists have less protection than car drivers. Passing too quickly can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other cars.
Street lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than road signs and other objects.

questions.question: When backing up, what is the best way to do it?

options.text: Steer with one hand and look in the rearview mirror.
Open the driver's door and look back.
Steer with both hands and look in the side mirror.
Steer with one hand and look over your shoulder through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer with one hand and look over your shoulder through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to look behind you before and while backing up. Use one hand to steer when backing up. Keep both hands on the wheel at all other times.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Side road.
Railroad warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood can affect your:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect your judgment and physical coordination. This makes it unsafe to drive, even if your blood alcohol level is below the legal limit.

questions.question: Which of these blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane:

options.text: The pedestrian must give you the right-of-way.
You must give them the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must give them the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No passing from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass from either direction. The only exceptions are making a left turn or passing pedestrians, bicyclists, scooter riders, or skateboard riders when the other lane is clear and safe.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea in bad weather.
Okay if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because frustrated drivers may try to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because frustrated drivers may try to pass you.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can cause drivers behind you to become impatient and take unsafe risks to pass you.

questions.question: You don't have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights if it is on a private road.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights on both public and private roads.

questions.question: What should you do if your tire blows out?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use your brakes right away.
Slowly reduce speed and pull to the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, take your foot off the gas and do not brake immediately. Slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and pull off the side of the road.

questions.question: Which statement about tires is true?

options.text: Tires must have good tread and be free of damage.
Low tire pressure makes the ride smoother.
Over-inflated tires do not skid on wet roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires must have good tread and be free of damage.
questions.explanation: Your tires must have good tread and no damage. Check your tires often.

questions.question: Can you use parking lights instead of headlights when driving at night?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive at night using only parking lights. You must use your headlights when visibility is low.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. What must you do?

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and doesn't take up the whole lane.
Honk to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder so you can pass.
Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a motorcycle, give it a full lane. Never share the same lane as a motorcycle. Moving back too quickly can force the rider to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic going straight. Always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. How do you prevent it in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down when driving on wet pavement.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting a highway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting a highway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: On a four-lane highway, where should slower traffic drive?

options.text: Center lane.
Right lane.
Left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane.
questions.explanation: On a four-lane highway, slower traffic should stay in the right lane. Use the left lanes to pass slower traffic.

questions.question: A car with bright headlights is driving toward you at night. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: When can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered when the light was green.
During rush hour traffic.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection is illegal and you can get a ticket.
